title: Function of the underlined sentence (science/history text)
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 15 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **15 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 7 Easy, 3 Medium, 5 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks for the function of the underlined sentence or portion 'in the text as a whole.' The passage is a science, research, or history text.
- The choices start with role verbs: 'It elaborates on,' 'It presents a finding,' 'It defines a term,' 'It summarizes the results,' 'It explains a method.'

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Ignore what the underlined part says and ask what it does for the sentence before and after it: is it background, a claim, a method, a result, an example, or a definition?
- 2) Check that the choice names the right idea it connects to.
- 3) Eliminate choices whose verb is too strong (dismisses, refutes) or that point to the wrong part of the text.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: A choice copies words from the underlined part but gives the wrong role, such as calling a result 'a method' or a researcher's finding 'the researcher's remarks.' Other choices have the relation wrong: 'dismisses the previous sentence' when the underlined part actually extends it.
You go by matching words, not by the role.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
